additional_sources_needed: GCS 66499.41(a)(8), for the exact demolition-protection test. Chaptered text of the statute on leginfo.legislature.ca.gov. It cannot be captured as evidence until a statute source type exists; do not capture it as an adopted_ordinance.
Los Angeles Housing Department records for RSO status, covenants, and Ellis Act withdrawals.
LADBS permit records for the five-year look-back.
candidate_pinpoint: Memo Part I, Demolition Protections, page 3 (GCS 66499.41(a)(8)); FAQ Q.14, page 17
candidate_excerpt: Specifically, a project may not be approved if it would require the demolition or alteration of any of the following types of housing:
locate_in_source: Located in shra-2025-10-28: Part I, Demolition Protections, pages 3-4 (GCS 66499.41(a)(8), the SB 1123 no-separation rule, and the Ellis Act bar); FAQ Q.14, page 17 (demolition and alteration). Vacancy is FAQ Q.1, page 12, and stays in la_shra.vacant-site-definition.
question_for_human_reviewer: The memo (pages 3-4) bars a project that would demolish or alter covenant-restricted, rent- or price-controlled, or recently tenant-occupied housing, and bars sites with an Ellis Act withdrawal within 15 years of the application. Do you agree with splitting the retired criterion into one criterion per protected category, a separate demolition-or-alteration judgment, and an Ellis Act criterion, with no category able to block from parcel facts alone?

proposed_controlled_interpretation.controlled_values_required: affordability-restricted-housing and price-controlled-housing (yes/no, controlled), ellis-act-withdrawal-recorded (yes/no, controlled). occupancy-history stays free text as professional input; existing-structures is professional input only.
proposed_controlled_interpretation.narrowing_note: Split on 2026-09-27 into la_shra.protected-housing-demolition-or-alteration, la_shra.protected-housing-affordability-covenant, la_shra.protected-housing-price-control, la_shra.protected-housing-tenant-occupancy, and la_shra.ellis-act-withdrawal, all pending human verification. No SHRA demolition criterion reads the structure count, so a structure is never a blocker. The SB 1123 no-separation rule is recorded as outside the screen.
proposed_controlled_interpretation.predicate_shape_if_reviewer_agrees: No component may block after review from parcel facts: each protected category and the Ellis Act record can only be consistent (absent) or route to judgment; tenant occupancy and demolition-or-alteration stay professional judgment.
must_remain_unresolved_when: occupancy history exists only as free text
a look-back period cannot be measured because no application date is recorded
protected housing is present and the project's demolition or alteration is unknown
structure, occupancy, RSO, covenant, or Ellis Act records conflict
proposed_controlled_interpretation.zimas_conflict_risk: Low to medium. The memo points to the ZIMAS eligibility checklist for the Ellis Act bar (page 4); ZIMAS stays observation-only unless the reviewer designates the LAHD record. A parcel display alone does not show occupancy history.

candidate_components.label: SHRA demolition or alteration of protected housing by the project
candidate_components.pinpoint: Memo Part I, Demolition Protections, page 3 (GCS 66499.41(a)(8)); FAQ Q.14, page 17

excerpts.text: Specifically, a project may not be approved if it would require the demolition or alteration of any of the following types of housing:
A demolition is the tearing down, razing or removal of a building or structure that requires a demolition permit.
Physical alterations include any construction or renovation to an existing structure other than a repair or addition.

candidate_components.controlled_value_encoding: No parcel fact: whether the project demolishes or alters protected housing depends on the project's scope.
judgment_or_ambiguity: FAQ Q.14 defines demolition and alteration; additions that change the existing structure count as alterations.
A structure count must never stand in: protected housing includes housing already demolished or vacated.
HCA and RPO replacement and the No Net Loss Declaration (page 4) are conditions, not bars.
candidate_components.reviewer_question: Do you agree that the demolition-or-alteration condition can never be decided from parcel records alone, so this criterion stays professional judgment even when every protected category is recorded absent?

candidate_components.label: SHRA protected housing: rent-restricted affordable housing on the parcel
candidate_components.pinpoint: Memo Part I, Demolition Protections, page 3 (GCS 66499.41(a)(8), category 1)

excerpts.text: Specifically, a project may not be approved if it would require the demolition or alteration of any of the following types of housing:
1) Housing that is subject to a recorded covenant, ordinance, or law that restricts rents to levels affordable to persons and families of low, very low, or extremely low income;

candidate_components.controlled_value_encoding: affordability-restricted-housing: yes/no from recorded covenants and City records.
candidate_components.proposed_rule_if_reviewer_agrees: false -> consistent_with_source (this protected category is absent). true -> requires_judgment (the bar applies only if the project would demolish or alter it; see la_shra.protected-housing-demolition-or-alteration). Never disqualifying_per_source from parcel facts.
judgment_or_ambiguity: The bar turns on the project, not the parcel.
Absence needs a complete covenant search; a failed search is unknown.
GCS 66499.41 is not captured; the memo summarizes it and says it does not include all applicable regulations (page 1).
candidate_components.reviewer_question: Do you agree that a complete record showing no covenant-, ordinance-, or law-restricted lower-income housing is consistent with this category, and that its presence can only route to the demolition-or-alteration judgment?

candidate_components.label: SHRA protected housing: rent- or price-controlled housing on the parcel
candidate_components.pinpoint: Memo Part I, Demolition Protections, page 3 (GCS 66499.41(a)(8), category 2)

excerpts.text: Specifically, a project may not be approved if it would require the demolition or alteration of any of the following types of housing:
2) Housing subject to any form of rent or sales price control imposed by a local public entity’s valid exercise of its police power (e.g., the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO)); or

candidate_components.controlled_value_encoding: price-controlled-housing: yes/no for any local rent or sales-price control. rso-status alone cannot answer it, because the RSO is one example.
candidate_components.proposed_rule_if_reviewer_agrees: false -> consistent_with_source (this protected category is absent). true -> requires_judgment (the bar applies only if the project would demolish or alter it). Never disqualifying_per_source from parcel facts.
judgment_or_ambiguity: 'Any form of rent or sales price control' is broader than the RSO.
AB 130 remainder parcels can retain existing housing (FAQ Q.23).
GCS 66499.41 is not captured; the memo summarizes it and says it does not include all applicable regulations (page 1).
candidate_components.reviewer_question: Do you agree that a record showing no housing under any local rent or sales-price control is consistent with this category, and which record should establish that absence beyond the RSO?

candidate_components.label: SHRA protected housing: tenant occupancy in the five years before the application
candidate_components.pinpoint: Memo Part I, Demolition Protections, page 3 (GCS 66499.41(a)(8), category 3)

excerpts.text: Specifically, a project may not be approved if it would require the demolition or alteration of any of the following types of housing:
3) Housing that has been occupied by a tenant within the five years prior to the application date, including, including housing that has been demolished or that tenants have vacated.

new_facts_needed: A dated tenant-occupancy record and the application date.
candidate_components.controlled_value_encoding: occupancy-history stays free text and is professional input only.
judgment_or_ambiguity: The five-year look-back runs from the application date, which a parcel screen does not have.
Housing since demolished or vacated counts; the memo notes permits since January 2023 may be reviewed (page 3).
Item 3 prints 'including, including'; read GCS 66499.41(a)(8) for the exact test.
candidate_components.reviewer_question: Should tenant occupancy in the five years before the application stay a Planning judgment, or can a dated, controlled occupancy record be designed once an application date is available?

candidate_components.label: SHRA Ellis Act withdrawal within 15 years of the application
candidate_components.pinpoint: Memo Part I, Demolition Protections, page 4

excerpts.text: In addition, the development may not be located on parcels where an Ellis Act withdrawal of units has occurred within 15 years of the application (see the ZIMAS eligibility checklist noted above).

new_facts_needed: ellis-act-withdrawal-date (the most recent withdrawal) and an application or evaluation date available to the predicate.
candidate_components.controlled_value_encoding: ellis-act-withdrawal-recorded: yes/no from a complete Los Angeles Housing Department record. A failed or incomplete lookup is unknown, never no.
candidate_components.proposed_rule_if_reviewer_agrees: false (complete reviewed LAHD record shows no withdrawal ever) -> consistent_with_source. true -> requires_judgment (the 15-year look-back runs from the application date, which the screen does not hold). Never disqualifying_per_source until a withdrawal date and an application date (or evaluation date) are modeled.
judgment_or_ambiguity: Measured from the application; the predicate signature has neither an application date nor the evaluation date.
Which Ellis Act event sets the date (notice filing or effective withdrawal) is not stated.
The memo points to the ZIMAS eligibility checklist; ZIMAS stays observation-only.
candidate_components.reviewer_question: Do you agree that a complete LAHD record showing no Ellis Act withdrawal is consistent with this bar, and that a recorded withdrawal must stay a judgment until both its date and the application date are recorded?

candidate_components.label: SB 1123: existing dwelling units not legally separated by the subdivision
candidate_components.pinpoint: Memo Part I, Demolition Protections, page 4 (SB 1123)

excerpts.text: Pursuant to SB 1123, any existing dwelling units on the property may not be legally separated as part of a SHRA subdivision.

candidate_components.controlled_value_encoding: No criterion ships; this constrains the subdivision design, not the site.
judgment_or_ambiguity: Existing units do not by themselves bar the site (see also FAQ Q.22 and Q.23).
candidate_components.reviewer_question: Do you agree the SB 1123 no-separation rule is a subdivision-design condition that the parcel screen should not evaluate?
